start.text: Still here. Still watching it. Mind my light.

first.text: An old man on an upturned fish box at the very end of the breakwater, baiting a hand line without looking at it. His eyes are on the grey out past the outer post.
Don't stand in my light. What there is of it.
Brenner. I fished the cod grounds forty-one years. Now I sit on a box and keep an eye on that, in case it gets ideas.

choice.text: Mara says you went out to the cod grounds.
What's out past the cod grounds?

watch.text: That. Came in off the sea the week after the Snuffing and lay down off the mouth, and it hasn't moved an inch since. I'd know. I've been sat here.
If it ever comes in over the wall, somebody ought to see it first and shout. Might as well be a man with nothing else to do.

cod.text: Second month after the Snuffing. A man's got to eat, and so has his harbor. I rowed out through that.
Came out the far side and fished. Good cod, the nets full. And I stood in the boat holding one up like a letter in somebody else's hand. Couldn't think what it was for.
Rowed home on the smell of the smokehouse. Mara met me at the post and took the fish off me. 'That's dinner, Brenner.' I said, 'What's dinner?'
Came back to me by morning. Most of it. I don't go out now.

choir.text: South. The Low Water: skerries and shallows you'd think you could wade, and the fog on it that sings. That one was there before the Snuffing. Always has been.
You row to the edge of it on a calm day and ship your oars and it's voices. A lot of them, near enough. None of them saying anything you can catch.

dare.text: Dunstan Tollen used to row out to the edge of it every spring, first calm day, for a dare. From fourteen. The last half backward, so he could see the singing coming.
I kept the tally for him. Notches on a stick. Mara never knew. Or knew and never said; that's Tollens.

after.text: Back again. Mind my light. There's more of it now.

after_first.text: An old man on an upturned fish box at the very end of the breakwater, baiting a hand line. His hand goes to his mouth now and then, for something that isn't there.
You'll be the one. The Gull. Brenner; I fished the cod grounds forty-one years, and I'd like to again.
Dropped my pipe in the harbor when she caught. Forty years I had that pipe. Never even looked where it went. I was looking at the Gull.
Odd thing. I used to hum something round the stem of it, mending. Pipe's gone and the tune with it, and I can't tell you which I miss.
Mended a net this morning. Good net. Started it in the middle, the way you'd start a sentence in the middle. Where else would you start one?

after_dunstan.text: Dunstan Tollen's home, and says he'll row me out to the cod grounds. Backward, I've no doubt.
Big fellow rowed in on the evening tide the other week, facing backward. Says he'll take me out to the cod grounds. I said yes before I'd thought. Felt like I owed him a yes.

choice.text: The grey's drawn back off the mouth.
Pell found a cork float with a mark burned in it.
What's out past the cod grounds?

leaned.text: Four boat-lengths. Young Tam paced it with an oar across the bow, and I held the boat for him, because his hands were shaking. Mine weren't. Mine were itching.
The cod grounds are just the far side of where it lies now. I can smell them. Mara says the Gull reaches so far and no farther, and I'm to wait and see how far.

choice.text: Go. The Gull's lit. It'll see you home.
Wait. Mara knows that light better than anyone.

leaned_go.text: That's what I wanted to hear, and I'll thank Mara not to hear you say it.
He winds the line back onto its winder, quick, the way a younger man would.

leaned_wait.text: ...Aye. I've waited this long. I'll see what the light's worth before I lean my weight on it.

float.text: A ring with a bar through it? That's my mark. My father's, before me.
Lost that whole string the day I went out through the grey. Never thought to see a cork of it again.
No. Leave it with the child. A lost thing ought to go to somebody that wants it, and nobody wants a cork float like a child does. I'll go along the shingle and tell them so.

choir_after.text: South. The Low Water: skerries and shallows, and the fog on it that sings. That one was there before the Snuffing. Always has been. The Gull looks right out over it.
You row to the edge of it on a calm day and ship your oars and it's voices. None of them saying anything you can catch.

dare_after.text: Dunstan Tollen used to row out to the edge of it every spring, for a dare. From fourteen. I kept the tally on a stick.
He's home now. I gave him the stick. He gave it back and said, 'Keep counting.'

dare_gull_after.text: He takes a short stick out of his gansey, notched all down one side, and turns it in his fingers.
Somebody used to row out to the edge of it every spring, for a dare. I kept the tally. Twenty-two notches, every one cut by me. Can't tell you for who.
Mara's been asking. I showed her the stick. She held it like it was warm.

home.text: An old man on an upturned fish box at the end of the breakwater, baiting a hand line. He looks at you as if you'd been gone a day.

home_released.text: Sat just where the Gull put it. No thicker, no thinner. Somebody sits up at the beacon of a night now, and I don't row past a thing that's keeping watch. Feels rude.
I went the once, like you told me, before you came home. Got my cod and knew what they were for. Once was enough to know.
I waited, like you told me. Still waiting. I'm getting good at it.

home_dark.text: Put my name on Mara's list. Fourth. She made me stand at the post and look at the grey first, and I looked, and I wrote.
What I've got left to burn is mostly cod and forty years of weather. They're welcome to choose.
I went out, the once, like you said. Glad of it. A man ought to know what he's putting his name to.
Never did go out. You said wait, and then there was nothing to wait for. I might, before midwinter. Just to have it.

choice.text: Pell found a cork float with your mark on it.
What's out past the cod grounds?

float_home.text: My mark, aye. Leave it with the child. A lost thing ought to go to somebody that wants it. I'll tell them so.
